chains.trait: Click train through melon and jaw
links: a fatty melon focuses broadband clicks, and a fat-filled channel in the lower jaw carries the returning echoes to the ear
in water sound travels about 1500 m/s, so echo delay resolves objects at centimetre scale
light fails within tens of metres in coastal water, so the only usable carrier is sound

skill.effect: The dolphin scans the surrounding waters, allowing you to clearly see hidden prey buried in the sand and other concealed targets nearby.

chains.weakness: it is listening, not looking: a loud broadband noise (engine, hammering, a bubble curtain) blanks the map for about 10 s and leaves it effectively blind
observe: a rounded fatty forehead with no beak above the eyes
a hollow, oil-filled jawbone you can feel through the skin
a fast accelerating click train that ends in a buzz just before a strike

journal.en: It sees with its forehead and hears with its chin.

plausibility.summary: 100 m full 3D map is optimistic for buried sand prey and clutter; use ~20–50 m high detail, 100 m coarse/localisation only in calm, low-noise water.
fixes: 100 m full 3D map is optimistic for buried sand prey and clutter; use ~20–50 m high detail, 100 m coarse/localisation only in calm, low-noise water.

analogues.organism: Tursiops truncatus biosonar — melon focusing, mandibular fat channel to ear (Au); oilbird/bat analogues for echolocation in lightless media, but cetacean receive path via jaw is distinctive
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded
see the cited works; chain wording is the council's own

links: each animal invents one individually distinctive frequency-modulated whistle and copies the versions of its partners
because it is learned and copied, the whistle is an arbitrary label for an individual, not a readout of mood
a group whose membership changes daily has to find specific partners again after hours apart and out of sight

skill.effect: The dolphin calls out a specific companion, which quickly answers and rejoins the group, even when visibility is poor.

chains.weakness: it answers to a name anyone can copy: play back its signature whistle and it will approach the speaker instead of its pod
observe: the same rising whistle shape repeated after every separation
two animals exchanging whistles and converging on each other
each individual with a different whistle contour, stable across days

journal.en: It gave itself a name, and it comes when you steal it.

plausibility.summary: 2 km summon is plausible for acoustic contact in open ocean but not guaranteed in noisy coastal habitat; add noise/habitat modifier halving range.
fixes: 2 km summon is plausible for acoustic contact in open ocean but not guaranteed in noisy coastal habitat; add noise/habitat modifier halving range.

analogues.organism: Bottlenose dolphin individually distinctive signature whistle, learned and copied — cohesion/identification (Janik & Slater; playback approach in Sayigh et al.)
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

chains.trait: One hemisphere asleep at a time
links: half the brain sleeps while the other half keeps watching and keeps the blowhole above water
breathing is a decision made at the surface, so full unconsciousness would be drowning
there is no safe surface and no burrow: the water column offers rest with no cover

skill.effect: The dolphin rests with half its mind awake, steadily recovering strength while remaining fully watchful for any approaching threats.

chains.weakness: it is never fully off duty: after three days without a genuine rest its reactions degrade, and any stun or entangle that stops it surfacing kills it outright
observe: one eye open, one closed, drifting in a slow circle
a surfacing rhythm that never varies, even at rest
an animal that never lies still on the bottom the way a seal can

journal.en: It has never once been fully asleep in its life.

analogues.organism: Cetacean unihemispheric slow-wave sleep (USWS) — blowhole vigilance while resting (Lyamin et al.; also fur seals/other marine mammals with variants)
analogues.mechanism: as named by the judge; no mechanism or reference recorded

relations.note: Same fluid physics, inverted solutions. Raven exploits low-density, transparent air for visual soaring and cache retrieval; dolphin exploits high-density, opaque water for active sonar and pressure-resistant diving. Playable: raven's visual tracking counters dolphin's acoustic stealth, while dolphin's sonar pierces raven's visual camouflage in fog.

Both solved fission-fusion sociality with vocal learning. Humans use speech and names; dolphins use signature whistles. Playable: players can teach dolphin pods human-like whistle patterns to coordinate group dives, or use human vocal mimicry to calm stressed pods.

Acoustic masking vs echolocation. Human vessel noise and seismic pulses scatter dolphin prey and mask signature whistles; dolphins counter by shifting click frequencies and using bubble curtains to break acoustic shadows. Playable: players can deploy low-frequency hums to disrupt dolphin sonar, or switch to silent hand signals to restore coordination.
